title: Семейный разговор в кабинете  (Family Talk in the Office)

segments.t: Chef Viktor Barinov proudly shows his daughter Katya around his new office at the Italian restaurant Arcobaleno. Katya casually asks her father to hire her, sparking a prickly family argument about why neither of them stayed in touch over the past year.
Я тебя и дольше не видела.
У меня всегда были свои причины.
Шеф, там картошку и помидоры привезли.
Let's examine the tense father-daughter conversation between Chef Barinov and Katya.
'Here are my new apartments.' Chef Barinov points out his office using a demonstrative particle and a plural possessive determiner.
'It is very cozy here in your place.' Katya uses an affectionate diminutive adverb to tease her father about the decor.
'Previously this office belonged to a woman.' The past-tense verb for was governs the instrumental masculine adjective modifying office.
'I see you have already settled in.' Katya pairs a first-person present verb with a masculine past reflexive verb.
'Of course, tell me how your life is.' Barinov prompts his daughter with an imperfective imperative verb.
'I am currently looking for a new job.' Katya uses the first-person singular present tense of to look for with a feminine accusative object.
'Dad, will you hire me to work with you?' A second-person future perfective verb turns her statement into a direct request.
'You did not call for a whole year!' Barinov scolds her using an accusative duration phrase and a negated feminine past verb.

'I have gone even longer without seeing you.' Katya counters with a comparative adverb and a negated past-tense verb.
У меня всегда были свои причины.
'I always had my own reasons.' Barinov defends himself with a plural past possession construction and a reflexive possessive determiner.
Шеф, там картошку и помидоры привезли.
'Chef, they delivered potatoes and tomatoes there.' Lyova interrupts with an impersonal plural past verb reporting a kitchen delivery.
'Do you not see that I am busy right now!' Barinov snaps at Lyova using a short masculine predicate adjective meaning busy.

'All right, Dad, I am leaving already.' Katya announces her departure in the first-person singular present tense. Now listen to the entire office scene between Chef Barinov, Katya, and Lyova without interruption.
